schema.description: Attribution tree via each concept's `topic` field; `edges` holds only prereq edges.

node_fields.name: concept name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.default_order: default teaching order within the topic
node_fields.visual: interactive | simulation | algorithm | function | chart | diagram | none (optional; absent = none)
node_fields.visual_hint: one-line description of what to show/manipulate; required when visual is set and != none

edge_types.prereq: from must be learned before to; strength=hard|soft

nodes.name: Network Layering
nodes.description: Decomposing network functionality into independent protocol layers, each providing services to the layer above and using the layer below, simplifying design and interoperability.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram the protocol-layer stack and how layers nest.

nodes.name: OSI Model
nodes.description: The seven-layer OSI reference model—physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, application—providing a conceptual framework for describing network protocol functions.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram the seven OSI layers and their roles.

nodes.name: TCP/IP Model
nodes.description: The practical Internet protocol stack of link, internet, transport, and application layers, organising the protocols that actually run the global Internet.

nodes.name: Encapsulation
nodes.description: The process by which each layer wraps data from the layer above in its own header, building nested protocol data units for transmission.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram each layer wrapping the layer above with its header.

nodes.name: Link Layer Services
nodes.description: Services the link layer provides over a single hop, including framing bits into packets and detecting transmission errors with checksums.

nodes.name: MAC Addressing
nodes.description: Media access control assigning hardware addresses to interfaces and arbitrating shared-medium access so multiple stations can transmit without persistent collisions.

nodes.name: Ethernet
nodes.description: The dominant wired LAN technology defining frame formats, MAC addressing, and historically CSMA/CD media access over switched links.

nodes.name: Switching
nodes.description: Layer-2 switches forwarding frames within a LAN by learning MAC-address-to-port mappings and flooding unknown destinations, building forwarding tables dynamically.

nodes.name: IP Addressing
nodes.description: Hierarchical IP addressing dividing addresses into network and host portions, with subnetting and CIDR enabling flexible allocation and route aggregation.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram an IP address split into network and host portions.

nodes.name: IPv4 and IPv6
nodes.description: The two Internet addressing versions: 32-bit IPv4 with its address exhaustion, and 128-bit IPv6 expanding the space and simplifying headers.

nodes.name: Forwarding and Routers
nodes.description: How routers forward packets by consulting a forwarding table to select an output interface using the destination address's longest prefix match.

nodes.name: Routing Algorithms
nodes.description: Distributed routing algorithms—link-state and distance-vector—by which routers exchange information to compute the paths that populate their forwarding tables.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate link-state/distance-vector routing building forwarding tables.

nodes.name: Transport Layer Services
nodes.description: End-to-end transport services running on hosts, multiplexing data to applications via ports and providing delivery semantics atop the network layer.

nodes.name: UDP
nodes.description: A connectionless transport protocol offering minimal, unreliable, unordered datagram delivery with low overhead, suited to latency-sensitive applications.

nodes.name: TCP
nodes.description: A connection-oriented transport protocol providing reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery using handshakes, sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and retransmission.
nodes.visual_hint: Sequence diagram of the TCP three-way handshake.

nodes.name: Transport Layer: Reliability and Control
nodes.name_zh: 传输层：可靠传输与拥塞控制

nodes.name: Reliable Data Transfer
nodes.description: Principles of reliable data transfer over unreliable channels using sequence numbers, acknowledgements, timeouts, and automatic repeat request (ARQ) protocols.
nodes.visual_hint: Sequence diagram of reliable transfer with sequence numbers and acks.

nodes.name: Flow Control
nodes.description: A receiver-driven mechanism using a sliding advertised window to prevent a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver's buffer.

nodes.name: Congestion Control
nodes.description: Sender-side algorithms that infer congestion from loss or delay and adjust the sending rate to share capacity fairly and avoid collapse.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot the TCP congestion window growing and backing off over time.

nodes.name: HTTP
nodes.description: The application-layer request-response protocol of the web, using methods, headers, and status codes to transfer resources, typically over TCP.

nodes.name: DNS
nodes.description: The Internet's distributed, hierarchical naming system that resolves human-readable hostnames into IP addresses through recursive and iterative queries.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram hierarchical DNS resolution of a hostname.

nodes.name: Other Application Protocols
nodes.description: Common application-layer protocols such as SMTP for email and FTP for file transfer, built atop transport services to deliver specific functions.
